newsitem.title: USA: N.Y. State Gov proposes $66 bln budget, up 2.2 pct.
newsitem.headline: N.Y. State Gov proposes $66 bln budget, up 2.2 pct.

text.p: New York State Gov. George Pataki unveiled Tuesday a $66.1 billion budget for fiscal 1998 that raises spending by 2.2 percent and includes an ambitious program of tax cuts coupled with more spending on schools.

Pataki estimated the state will end the 1997 fiscal year on March 31 with a $1.3 billion surplus, which mainly will be used to slash the $2.3 billion projected budget gap for the following fiscal year to about $1.3 billion.

Pataki, whose previous budget was sharply criticized by fiscal monitors for relying too heavily on nonrecurring items, called one-shots, noted that the fiscal 1998 budget only calls for $66 million of this type of measure.

"This stands in sharp contrast to the record level of 'one-shot' actions over the last decade, which peaked at $1.9 billion in 1990-91," the governor said, in prepared remarks. This was a reference to the former Cuomo Administration.

The Republican governor, who is known for his fiscal austerity, added, "This balanced plan builds a brighter future by providing for the people what they need and expect from the state government and a cost the people can afford, and not a nickel more."

The new budget also calls for raising the total spent on welfare by $414 million to $5.49 billion, with the state benefiting from a 250,000 drop in welfare caseloads since January 1995. As a result of this drop, New York State will get an extra $280 million in federal welfare aid in fiscal 1997 and 1998. Pataki has proposed a new welfare plan, needed to comply with the federal overhaul of welfare that became law last summer, but the legislature has yet to take the measure up.

The budget includes a $3.4 billion program to cut school property taxes for New York homeowners by 27 percent over four years. Spending on education is budgeted to rise $302 million to total $10.57 billion.
